narrative.overview:
Mechanical Librarian feels like a carefully kept private reading room where every book, note, and decision has a precise place. The interface is calm, exact, editorial, and quietly domestic: warm paper planes, green-black ink, restrained archive teal, and serif bibliographic emphasis make operational work feel considered without disguising its technical authority.

The system remains dense enough for serious review, but hierarchy comes from typography, spacing, borders, and tonal layers rather than dashboard spectacle. Glossy SaaS chrome, playful consumer-library styling, decorative gradients, and attention-seeking motion are anti-references.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper surfaces with a semantic, fully paired dark theme.
Editorial serif emphasis inside a compact sans-serif operating system.
Thin catalogue-like rules, restrained controls, and rounded reading surfaces.
Archive teal for current selection and affirmative action; ochre and red for exceptional states.
Responsive task continuity from wide workspaces to a 320px minimum viewport.

rules.name: The Marginalia Rule
rules.body: Color annotates state; it does not decorate empty space. Archive teal identifies the current or affirmative path, ochre calls for care, and red is reserved for failure or destructive consequence.

rules.name: The Semantic Pairing Rule
rules.body: Light and dark themes preserve role and hierarchy, not literal brightness relationships. Never substitute an unpaired hue when switching themes.

rules.name: The Catalogue Voice Rule
rules.body: Use serif type for bibliographic identity, decision values, and measured emphasis. Use sans-serif type for everything the owner must operate, scan, or verify.

rules.name: The Borders-Before-Shadows Rule
rules.body: Establish grouping with tone and a one-pixel border. Add shadow only when a surface actually floats, overlaps, or must remain consequential while content moves beneath it.

dos: Do use warm paper, ink, and catalogue lines as the default hierarchy.
Do reserve Archive Teal for current selection, affirmative action, and calm recorded state.
Do keep every interactive target at least 44px high and preserve the three-pixel offset focus outline.
Do keep task identity and direct values in serif type while operational controls and evidence remain sans-serif.
Do collapse wide workspaces into explicit, continuous mobile tasks rather than squeezing desktop columns.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion; state changes must remain understandable with animation effectively removed.
donts: Don't use color as ambient decoration or introduce an unpaired theme hue.
Don't add shadow to a surface that does not float, overlap, or remain consequential while scrolling.
Don't turn every control or container into a pill; pills are reserved for navigation, lenses, and compact state.
Don't imitate a glossy analytics dashboard, playful bookshelf app, or cover-led streaming catalogue.
Don't fabricate cover art where the interface only has initials or target identity.
Don't add attention-seeking motion; the incumbent system uses motion only as a reducible state transition.
